xrayTube.moseleyTitle: Moseley plot of the Kα lines
xrayTube.shellTitle: Inner shells of the anode atom
xrayTube.belowEdge: eV is below the K-shell binding energy: no K lines
xrayTube.aboveEdge: A K electron is knocked out: K lines are emitted

pairProduction.nothingTakes: Nothing is there to take the difference.

annihilation.onePhotonForbiddenPattern: Forbidden: {{deficit}} of momentum has nowhere to come from.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a photon striking an electron at rest, the scattered photon and the recoiling electron, the triangle formed by their momenta, a table of measurements, and a graph.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets the incident photon's energy, the scattering angle, whether the target has bound electrons, and which graph is shown. A detector can be fired at to build an energy spectrum.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the scattering angle and compare the scattered wavelength with the incident one.

compton.currentDetailsPattern: A photon of energy {{energy}} and wavelength {{wavelength}} scatters through {{angle}}. Its wavelength grows by {{shift}} to {{scatteredWavelength}}, and its energy falls to {{scatteredEnergy}}. The electron recoils at {{recoilAngle}} from the beam with {{kinetic}} of kinetic energy.

controls.energyHelp: Sets the photon energy on a logarithmic scale from 1 electronvolt to 10 megaelectronvolts.
controls.presetHelp: Sets the incident photon to this source.
controls.angleHelp: Angle between the incident and the scattered photon, from 0 to 180 degrees.
controls.graphHelp: Chooses the graph: wavelength shift against angle, a spectrometer at the chosen angle, or the energy spectrum of a detector.
controls.firePhotonsHelp: Sends photons into the detector and counts the energy each one deposits.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows an X-ray tube with electrons crossing from the cathode to the anode, the inner shells of an anode atom, and the spectrum of the X-rays produced.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets the tube voltage, the tube current, the anode metal, and whether the spectrum is plotted against wavelength or photon energy. A Moseley plot can be shown.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Raise the voltage and watch the short-wavelength limit move while the characteristic lines stay where they are.

xrayTube.currentDetailsPattern: A {{target}} anode at {{voltage}} kilovolts. No photon has a wavelength shorter than {{minimumWavelength}} or an energy above {{maximumEnergy}}. Characteristic lines present: {{lines}}.

controls.voltageHelp: Accelerating voltage between cathode and anode, in kilovolts.
controls.currentHelp: Number of electrons reaching the anode each second. Changes the intensity of the whole spectrum, not its shape.
controls.anodeHelp: Chooses the metal the electrons strike.
controls.axisHelp: Plots the spectrum against wavelength or against photon energy.
controls.presetHelp: Sets the voltage and anode of this example.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a photon arriving from the left, the electron and positron it may produce, and bars comparing the energy and the momentum before and after.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets the photon energy, whether a nucleus is nearby, how the kinetic energy is shared between the electron and the positron, and whether a magnetic field curves their tracks.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Lower the photon energy below 1.022 megaelectronvolts, then remove the nucleus.

pairProduction.productsPattern: The electron takes {{electronKinetic}} and the positron {{positronKinetic}} of kinetic energy. The nucleus takes {{nucleusMomentum}} of momentum and only {{nucleusKinetic}} of energy.

controls.energyHelp: Photon energy in megaelectronvolts. A pair needs at least 1.022.
controls.presetHelp: Sets the photon energy to this value.
controls.surroundingsHelp: Chooses whether the photon passes near a lead nucleus, near a carbon nucleus, or travels through empty space.
controls.share: Electron's share of the kinetic energy
controls.shareHelp: Percentage of the available kinetic energy carried by the electron. The positron takes the rest.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a positron meeting an electron at rest and the two photons that leave, a table of their energies and directions, and a ring of detectors around a tracer.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets the positron's kinetic energy and the direction in which the photons are emitted, and offers a single-photon alternative. The scanner can record annihilations and the tracer can be hidden.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Start with the positron at rest, then give it kinetic energy and watch the photons stop being back to back.

annihilation.currentDetailsPattern: A positron with {{kinetic}} of kinetic energy annihilates with an electron at rest. Photon 1 carries {{energy1}} at {{angle1}}, photon 2 carries {{energy2}} at {{angle2}}. The angle between them is {{opening}}.

controls.kineticHelp: Kinetic energy of the positron in megaelectronvolts. Zero is annihilation at rest.
controls.cmAngleHelp: Direction of photon 1 in the centre-of-momentum frame, measured from the positron's direction of travel.
controls.petRunHelp: Starts or stops the scanner. Each annihilation adds a line between the two detectors that fired.
controls.tracerHelp: Move the tracer inside the detector ring with the arrow keys or by dragging.
controls.tracerValuePattern: Tracer {{x}} centimetres right and {{y}} centimetres up from the centre of the ring.
